why_this_supersedes_nothing: C8 and C9 measure different properties of the same machinery -- C8 that the run POINTER does not decide the consume, C9 that CONTENTION does not produce two of them -- so neither retires the other and both must keep describing the working tree.
obligation: D-065 obligation 1: atomically bind one agent to one run, assignment and digest. The external audit marked it only PARTIALLY discharged, with the named gap 'atomic concurrent-stop behavior not independently rerun within the safety boundary'. Deterministic wrong-agent, wrong-assignment, changed-assignment and changed-byte cases were all tested; the RACE the O_EXCL claim exists for was not. This canary runs it.
method: 24 SubagentStop processes were started and each blocked on a read from one FIFO, so none could proceed until a single write released them all together -- the release is simultaneous rather than staggered by process spawn time. Every process was given byte-identical event JSON naming the same agent, the same assignment and the same proof, against ONE open receipt.
THE_MEASURED_PROPERTY: 24 simultaneous dispatches produced exactly 1 consumed row. That row is the write-attribution record, so exactly one agent-to-result binding exists no matter how many stops arrive at once.
why_five_were_accepted_and_only_one_cons: 19 processes were refused by the in-flight consume claim, naming the agent already inside the consume path. 5 serialised through: the first found the receipt open and consumed it, and the rest found it already consumed WITH A MATCHING RESULT DIGEST and were accepted idempotently. Idempotent re-acceptance is the documented behaviour and is not a second admission: it writes no ledger row, takes no claim, and records no new attribution. The count that matters is the consumed row, and there is one.
resolution_limit: One trial at one width on one filesystem. It demonstrates that the claim held under real contention here; it is not a proof of atomicity, and NFS or overlay lock semantics are untested.
what_this_does_not_claim: Nothing about the shared-OS-user residual: every process here was cooperative and honest. A deliberately misbehaving agent can still forge repo-local artifacts, and no number of race trials speaks to that. It moves no gate.

obligation_2_measurement.why: The external audit marked D-065 obligation 2 -- hard Start failure on lease or receipt creation failure -- only PARTIALLY discharged, with the named gap 'end-to-end live Start behavior was NOT_EXECUTED_SAFETY_BOUNDARY'. It is executed here.
obligation_2_measurement.method: The lease directory was made unwritable (chmod 500, restored immediately afterwards; it is gitignored and holds no tracked file). A control dispatch with the directory writable leased normally FIRST, so the failure below is attributable to the permission change and not to the agent id. Then a dispatch was run with everything else valid: a real minted receipt, a real assignment, a contract-valid result, and a correct admission proof. The ONLY defect was the missing Start-time lease.
obligation_2_measurement.start_injected_warning: Run lease: NOT RECORDED (PermissionError); SubagentStop will block this agent
obligation_2_measurement.stop_reason: No Start-time run lease exists for this agent, so its run identity cannot be established. Refusing to fall back to the mutable ACTIVE_RUN pointer. Re-run the agent after confirming that SubagentStart can write .agent-harness/leases/.
obligation_2_measurement.WHAT_WAS_MEASURED: Start does NOT exit non-zero on a lease-write failure. It exits 0, records the failure in the context it injects into the agent, and states that Stop will block. That promise HOLDS: with every other input valid, Stop refused with 'No Start-time run lease exists for this agent, so its run identity cannot be established. Refusing to fall back to the mutable ACTIVE_RUN pointer.' No consume occurred.
obligation_2_measurement.WHAT_IS_NOT_CLAIMED: The obligation is worded 'hard Start failure'. What is demonstrated is the EFFECT -- no agent reaches admission without a lease -- achieved by fail-forward at Start plus refusal at Stop, not by Start itself failing hard. Whether that wording is satisfied by the effect is an adjudicator's call and is not decided here. The single writer who ran the measurement does not get to grade it.

refused_result_artifact.why_it_is_not_retained: This envelope was the discriminator's INPUT -- a contract-valid result proving that the missing lease was the only defect -- and its dispatch was correctly REFUSED, so it was never admitted. An unattributed result artifact whose open receipt sits outside the active run is left-over state by validate_harness's own definition, and leaving it would make the harness fail on every future commit. Its digest is recorded here and its `minted` row stays in ADMISSIONS.jsonl, so the fact that it existed and was refused survives; the mutable file does not.

why_the_result_envelope_says_PENDING: A structural constraint, discovered by the checker rather than by design, and recorded because it applies to every future measuring canary. The result envelope must EXIST before the dispatch, because the dispatch is what consumes it -- and the Stop hook pins its SHA-256 into the ledger at consume time. So a canary that measures the dispatch cannot describe the outcome in its own envelope: the outcome does not exist yet, and writing it afterwards changes bytes the ledger has already pinned. The first attempt here did exactly that, and check_canary_freshness.py refused it with 'The ledger row and the artifact disagree' -- the re-hash catching the writer, which is what it is for. The envelope was restored to the consumed bytes, and the measured outcome lives here, in an artifact the ledger does not pin and which is therefore free to be written last.
